title: Allocation spectral fingerprinting and defrag strategies
content:
TL;DR:
We used a lightweight "spectral" profiling approach (continuous allocation-size histograms over sliding windows) to correlate allocation fingerprints with downstream OOMs and high tail latency. The signal shows a recurring mid-size allocation pattern (8–24MiB) that interacts poorly with our slab buckets and the K/V cache growth, causing high fragmentation and cudaMalloc stalls on heavy tails.

Background and motivation:
- Problem: intermittent OOMs and long cudaMalloc stall times on multi-tenant Dedicated pools under bursty chat workloads.
- Existing notes cover allocator arena sizing, general fragmentation hypotheses, and KV cache growth, but we lacked a concise way to tie allocation *shape* to runtime failure modes across requests.
- Goal: produce a compact diagnosis method (spectral fingerprint), reproduce the spike, and propose pragmatic mitigations for short-term and medium-term rollout.

What we measured (approach):
1) Continuous allocation-size histogram (per-GPU, per-process, 1s buckets, 1m sliding window). Capture count and bytes for size bins: <4KiB, 4–64KiB, 64KiB–1MiB, 1–8MiB, 8–24MiB, 24–64MiB, >64MiB.
2) Metadata: uptime, resident set, live KV-cache token counts, active streams, allocator fallback counts (cudamalloc vs cudamallocasync), decommit events.
3) Correlate with request traces: request id, model, seq_len, num_tokens_generated, serve-path (hosted/dedicated/private).

Key observations:
- Before OOMs we observed a distinct bump in the 8–24MiB bin lasting ~10–40s; simultaneously the >64MiB bin showed sporadic large allocations but not frequent enough to explain OOM by itself.
- Allocation-rate (allocs/s) in the small-to-medium bins increased throughout the minute leading up to the failure; free-rate lagged behind -> transient working set grew.
- KV-cache growth (by token-weighted size) correlates with the medium-bin bump. The cache holds many ephemeral entries from beam-search-like reranking requests.
- cudaMalloc retries and the host-side stall metric grew nonlinearly once fragmentation exceeded ~70% of usable pool in our mempool simulation.
- Single request tails: requests that triggered OOM often had an early-medium allocation spike (workspace + temporary buffers) then series of small allocations for logits/attention caching.

Hypothesis (concise):
- Medium-sized ephemeral allocations (8–24MiB) create fragmentation holes between slab bucket boundaries; combined with oversized slabs for >64MiB allocations and KV-cache growth, the allocator cannot find contiguous blocks for large workspace allocations, triggering cudaMalloc fallback/retries and eventual OOM.

Reproduction steps (fast repro):
1) Use workload-sim binary: workloads/repro/spike-generator --model gpt-medium --kv-load 0.8 --burst-pattern "40s-on,20s-off" --token-dist heavy-rerank 
2) Run on a Dedicated GPU node with mempool enabled and default slab sizes (see env: MEMPOL_SLAB_SIZES=4K,64K,1M,8M,48M).
3) Observe allocation histograms (script: tools/alloc_histstream.sh) and watch for 8–24MiB bin growth.
4) Trigger load from 50 concurrent sessions ramped in 10s; OOM typically manifests within 90–220s in our lab.

Telemetry queries and dashboards to create:
- Query (pseudo-SQL): SELECT bin, SUM(count) as allocs, SUM(bytes) as bytes, timestamp FROM gpu_alloc_hist WHERE gpu_id=$GPU GROUP BY bin, timestamp ORDER BY timestamp DESC;
- Derived: compute fragmentation_ratio = 1 - (largest_free_contiguous / total_free). Alert when fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 and medium-bin bytes > X (configurable by pool size).
- Add a per-request trace tag when a cudaMalloc fallback/retry happens; pipe these into flame graphs for tail analysis.

Experiments run and results (short log):
- Experiment A: reduce slab boundary at medium sizes (add 12MiB bucket). Result: reduced fragmentation ratio by ~18% and cudaMalloc retries dropped 2x in repro. Tail latency improved ~14% for 99.9th percentile.
- Experiment B: aggressive KV-cache trimming (LRU threshold lowered). Result: KV footprint dropped 22%, but overall token throughput decreased 6% on workloads that benefit from cached reranks.
- Experiment C: cooperative defrag (defer small frees to batch coalesce). Result: lower frequency of contiguous-free windows — marginal improvement but introduced small latency jitter for small requests.

Short-term mitigations (safe to roll quickly):
- Add a medium slab bucket (12MiB) and tweak slab sizing for pools with high rerank traffic. Rollout path: feature flag mempool.medium_bucket=true, start with Dedicated staging pool.
- Implement eviction-aware KV-cache trimming under high-fragmentation signals (threshold-based, not purely LRU).
- Increase warning telemetry: emit fragmentation_ratio and medium-bin bytes as per-node metrics and drive ephemeral alerts (SLO error budget only).

Medium-term fixes (Q1 roadmap):
- Defragmentation pass: implement background coalescer that opportunistically merges adjacent free spans during low-util periods. Must be careful with cuda context and pinned buffers; requires allocator support.
- Allocation fingerprinting alerting (automated): when specific spectral signatures (e.g., medium-bin ramp + KV growth) detected, automatically reduce KV-cache aggressiveness + enable medium slab bucket on that host.
- Smarter placement for K/V cache: consider partitioning cache into separate arena to avoid interference with large workspace allocations. This is more invasive but isolates cross-workload interference.

Questions / unknowns / risks:
- Risk that medium slab bucket reduces memory availability for other buckets and increases overhead; need pool-level simulation across full request mix.
- Background defrag may interact poorly with pinned memory and CUDA swap patterns; need a safe stopgap (no direct free during in-flight cudamalloc).
- Will adding buckets increase amortized fragmentation in different workloads? Need long-tail evaluation across multi-day runs.

Next actions (owners):
- Aisha: run pool-level simulator with mixed traffic matrix and new slab config (deadline: 2024-11-27).
- Diego: add the spectral histogram metric to our per-GPU exporter and a Grafana panel (2024-11-22).
- Marcus: prototype medium-slab feature-flag in mempool and run repro on staging (2024-11-24).
- Priya: prepare rollout plan for Dedicated with a rollback strategy and communication note for CSM (2024-11-29).

Appendix (quick notes and snippets):
- alloc_histstream.sh (pseudo):
  while true; do curl -s $METRIC_ENDPOINT/gpu/$GPU/hist | jq .bins >> /tmp/alloc_hist.$GPU; sleep 1; done

- repro command example:
  MEMPOL_SLAB_SIZES=4K,64K,1M,8M,48M ./workloads/repro/spike-generator --model gpt-medium --kv-load 0.8 --concurrency 50

- Quick regression metric: 99.9th latency pre/post medium-bucket patch on staging.

Notes-to-self (incomplete thoughts):
- Consider a lightweight simulation that models contiguous free-run length distribution; can be cheaper than full mempool sim.
- Check interplay with cudamemset and any pinned-host allocations from host-side caching.
- If we expose bucket config per-customer, ops complexity may increase but gives flexibility.

End of note.
